subject: Hosted API: locality, TTL and purge controls — security questionnaire responses
messages:
From: Amy Lin <amy.lin@verdantcloud.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Verdant Cloud Security <security@verdantcloud.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T16:12:00Z
Subject: Hosted API - questions on data locality, TTL, and deletion controls

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for agreeing to answer a few items from our security questionnaire. We need concise, auditable answers for the following items related to Redwood's Hosted API (Verdant is evaluating for production use):

1) Where is customer request payload and generated output stored (region)? Do you offer region pinning / geofencing for hosted API customers?
2) What are default retention windows for: ingestion/request payloads, generated outputs, debug logs, and audit logs? Are any of these configurable per-tenant?
3) Describe the deletion workflow when a tenant requests erasure (time to remove from live stores, caches, backups, and logs).
4) Are backups replicated cross-region by default? If so, what controls exist to opt-out?
5) What evidence can Redwood provide (attestations, SOC2 artifact, sample audit log extract) and how soon?

Appreciate numbered answers so our GRC team can map them to our control matrix. If anything needs product review, loop them in.

Regards,
Amy

Head of Security Programs
Verdant Cloud

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Amy Lin <amy.lin@verdantcloud.com>
Cc: Verdant Cloud Security <security@verdantcloud.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-29T21:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Hosted API - questions on data locality, TTL, and deletion controls

Hi Amy — thanks for the clear list. Answers below numbered to match your questionnaire. I kept responses precise and included links and two attachments (retention matrix and SOC2 summary). Happy to jump on a short call to walk through.

1) Region / locality
- Customer request payloads and generated outputs for the Hosted API are processed in the region you select at provisioning (we support us, eu, apac regions). Default routing is regional.
- We offer region pinning (geofencing) for tenant data on Hosted plans via account configuration; requests can be restricted to a single region for both compute and persistent logs.

2) Default retention windows (Hosted API)
- Request payloads / generation outputs: by default stored for up to 14 days for troubleshooting and quality monitoring.
- Debug/trace logs: retained 30 days by default.
- Audit logs (auth events, admin actions): retained 90 days by default.
- Configurability: retention windows for payloads and debug logs are configurable for enterprise accounts and for Dedicated/Private customers. Hosted customers can request retention exceptions via contract (e.g., shorter retention) and we can apply tenant-level policies in most regions.

3) Deletion / erasure workflow
- On an erasure request we: (a) remove tenant identifiers from live indexes and mark tenant data for immediate purge from active stores within 48 hours; (b) clear in-memory caches and KV cache entries on the next cache cycle (generally within minutes to one hour); (c) initiate background deletion for persisted objects (completed within 72 hours in normal operating conditions); (d) backup snapshots are retained according to backup retention policy (see #4) — backups containing the tenant are flagged and removed per the backup removal process (typically within 30 days unless under legal hold).
- Audit log retention follows the configured audit retention policy; filtered extracts can be provided on request as part of incident response.

4) Backups and cross-region replication
- Backups are created daily for operational recovery. Cross-region replication is NOT enabled by default for Hosted tenants — replication is only enabled for accounts that opt into multi-region high availability (this is part of Dedicated/enterprise configuration or a Hosted add-on).
- To opt-out: Hosted customers are not replicated cross-region unless they sign up for multi-region HA; existing customers requesting removal from replicated backups are handled via our backup remove workflow and documented change request.

5) Evidence and artifacts
- We can provide: SOC 2 Type II summary (attached), system architecture diagram for regional controls, sample redacted audit log extracts, and a retention matrix mapping categories to stores and TTLs (attached). For formal requests we provide an Evidence Package through a secure share link.

Notes:
- Encryption: all data at-rest is encrypted with keys managed by our KMS; customer-managed KMS/HSM is available for Private and Dedicated customers on request.
- Logs: request-level logs are indexed with tenant IDs for observability and can be scoped/scoped removals applied per erasure requests.
- Exceptions: legal holds or active investigations may delay complete purge; we will notify the customer and provide timelines.

Please see attached files (redwood-retention-matrix-v2.xlsx, redwood-soc2-summary-2028-01.pdf). If you want a formal attestation or a signed artifact we can schedule a short review with our GRC team.

Best,
